newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil seen up $1, Brent IPE up 5 cents.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil seen up $1, Brent IPE up 5 cents.

text.p: IPE gas oil futures were expected to start $1 to $1.50 higher on Tuesday, and IPE Brent to begin some five cents up on a follow through to late short covering before Monday's close, brokers said.
Gas oil closed on Monday at $161.25 a tonne, missing out on crude's late recovery into positive territory, and will be catching up. Brent settled on Monday at $18.18 a barrel.

Dealers said they would be looking for indications on when Iraq would present the U.N. with the aid plan it needs to clear before crude exports could resume, and also at energy stocks data due out later on Tuesday.

International Energy Agency data predicting weaker prices later this year, despite a rise in demand, may weigh on the market, dealers said, but more attention will be focused on Tuesday's American Petroleum Institute stock figures.
"I think we will be quietly firm today ahead of the APIs," said one broker, who added that the market was expecting a draw of 2-3 million barrels in U.S. crude inventories.
IPE Brent bounced off support at $18 on Monday, which was a cue for late buying by local dealers that moved prices high in thin volumes.

In New York, West Texas Intermediate futures settled at $19.52, some three cents down. They had traded lower for most of the day but recovered on the back of London buying, breaking back through the $18.40 a barrel support level.
